```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Willingness to pay is better evidenced and much higher. A cites seven live competitors with published B2B prices of $29.99–$124/month. B's comparables sit at $3.99–$7/month, and one of B's own demand quotes says users want it 'free to use' because 'caregivers are usually financially stressed.'",
    "A's pain is quantified in the buyer's own words: '1-2 hours' every evening writing quotes, with a sourced Reddit link. That is a business cost a contractor can justify paying to remove. B's pain is spreadsheets and group texts, which users already solve for free.",
    "A has a lighter regulatory burden for a solo operator: hosted Stripe for PCI SAQ-A scope plus a templated privacy policy. B carries possible FTC Health Breach Notification Rule exposure and ongoing Washington My Health My Data Act obligations, which include a private right of action, all on a sub-$10/month product.",
    "B's structure works against early revenue. Its brief documents three problems: activation depends on siblings adopting the app, customer lifetime ends when care ends, and incumbents already win the organic Reddit channel with unsolicited recommendations. A single contractor can buy and use A's product alone.",
    "Both fields are crowded, with 7 direct competitors in A versus 6 in B, so crowding does not separate them. The difference is that each A customer is worth roughly 10–20x more per month, which leaves more room to absorb acquisition cost."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's lead demand quote ('Google Calendar and group threads weren't really built for caregiving. That's why I built [an app]...') comes from a founder promoting their own app, not from a prospective payer. It shows supply-side interest, not willingness to pay. B's other sourced quote actively argues against payment ('As long as it's free to use').",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. A has real gaps. Its second demand quote has no retrieved URL, so it counts as missing, leaving only one sourced demand quote. Its $237 CPL figure is a generic B2B SaaS benchmark, not specific to contractors. Its claims that EstimationPro and Outdoor Estimates were built by single founders, and that no competitor dominates, are not sourced. Several competitor prices are also unpublished. A still wins because its sourced pricing and quantified pain point more clearly to a first paying customer within 90 days than B's low-price, free-expectation consumer market."
}
```
